card.name: Belly dance
card.era: ancient roots; term coined 1860s; Egyptian classical form 20th century
card.tagline: Torso-driven dance of hip and abdomen articulations
card.profile: Belly dance is the Western name (from the French danse du ventre, coined in the 1860s) for a torso-driven dance emphasising articulations of the hips and torso, with Egypt's forms the most recognised worldwide. Per Wikipedia, in Egypt it has two contexts: the social/folk raqs baladi danced by ordinary people at celebrations, and the professional raqs sharqi of cabarets and film. It isolates the torso muscles rather than moving the limbs through space, distinguishing it from many Western dance forms.
card.insight: Belly dance is among the most globally widespread Middle Eastern dance forms, though it remains contested within parts of the Arab world; Egyptian cinema spread its imagery worldwide (Wikipedia).
